newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds mostly flat, seek direction.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds mostly flat, seek direction.

text.p: Most prices of U.S. mortgage-backed securities were at par to two ticks lower and spreads to Treasuries barely budged in a quiet session on Wednesday.
With no economic data to stir any excitement, some market participants continued to dabble in dollar rolls, traders said.
"The only action today was in the Fannie 8.0 percent rolls," said one pass-through trader, referring to players trying to cover their short positions in April with bonds in May.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent paper was off 1/32 at 100-23/32 bid, yielding 118 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were 1/32 lower as well, at 100-23/32 bid and 100-30/32 bid, respectively.
The five-year Treasury note was down 2/32 at 99-13/32 bid to yield 6.77 percent, and the 10-year Treasury note was off 3/32 to yield 6.90 percent.
Traders said yield spreads for the past week have been stuck in narrow range -- about 37.5 basis points.
"Until we get some more economic news, we will be in that range," said on Ginnie trader in New York.
He said spreads may break out of that range if retail sales and producer prices in March, slated for release on Friday, defy market expectations.
Economists in a Reuters poll forecast the March headline producer price index and retail sales figures to be unchanged and 0.6 percent higher, respectively.
